purpose: Known-answer canonical fold/cusp oscillatory-integral fixtures for validating finite-frequency caustic kernels before connecting them to Kerr arrival-time surfaces.
claim_ceiling: These are universal canonical catastrophe integrals, not Kerr lensing results. Their values do not validate a Kerr arrival-time surface, source normalization, polarization, or astrophysical amplification factor.

conventions.integration_domain: real line, interpreted as an oscillatory integral under the declared symmetric/contour prescription
conventions.precision: reference decimals computed at 80 decimal digits; retain expression identities as the primary oracle
conventions.complex_representation: real and imaginary components are recorded separately

required_checks: imaginary part is zero within the declared quadrature error for real u
oscillatory quadrature converges under domain/contour refinement
stationary-phase asymptotics are recovered far from the fold in their valid sectors

cusp.integral_identity: Pearcey(0,0) = integral_R exp(i*t^4/4) dt = Gamma(1/4)/sqrt(2) * exp(i*pi/8)
required_checks: complex integral agrees with the gamma-function identity at (X,Y)=(0,0)
oscillatory quadrature converges under symmetric-domain and contour refinement
cusp response remains finite through the canonical caustic core
fold-locus asymptotics are recovered under the appropriate parameter scaling

recommended_independent_references: gamma-function identity for the Pearcey origin
